subject.title: fix(clawhub): keep request deadline through response body

question: Should the existing 30-second ClawHub request timeout become a hard wall-clock limit for large archive downloads, or should archives keep a distinct transfer-lifetime policy?
rationale: Both choices are implementable, but they define user-visible install compatibility: a universal deadline prevents endless drips while also terminating healthy slow transfers that current main permits.

options.title: Separate archive transfer policy
options.body: Keep the hard total deadline for JSON and small bodies, but give archives a longer or throughput-aware transfer budget with slow-progress success coverage.

options.title: Adopt the universal 30-second limit
options.body: Intentionally cap all ClawHub bodies at 30 seconds and add documentation plus representative healthy large-download proof showing the limit is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Separate archive transfer policy
recommendation.body: Keep the hard total deadline for JSON and small bodies, but give archives a longer or throughput-aware transfer budget with slow-progress success coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged ClawHub policy work makes this person the best available routing candidate for the compatibility choice.
